behaviour-switch.answer: The switch is DialectBehavior.CompileTimeArithmeticImplementorDefined (src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime/Control/DialectBehavior.cs:301): before 2023 compile-time arithmetic expressions use standard arithmetic (§2002:7.2.5.2 GR1 'Standard arithmetic shall be used for all arithmetic operations'), and such expressions occur only in DEFINE and EVALUATE directives, constant conditional expressions and constant entries (§2002:7.2.5); its only call sites are the >>DEFINE/>>IF/>>EVALUATE evaluator and the constant-entry binder (git grep CompileTimeArithmetic in src). This directive's format carries only keywords or comment-text, no compile-time arithmetic expression, so the switch cannot reach the rule; >>SOURCE FORMAT takes only FIXED or FREE. At --std 2002 a directive on line 1 is accepted in either form: written in free form (column 1) by srcfmt-first-free.cob (FIRST-LINE-FREE) and srcfmt-first-free-to-fixed.cob (FREE-FORM-FIRST-TO-FIXED), written in fixed form (program-text area) by srcfmt-first-fixed.cob (FIRST-LINE-FIXED-FORM), all run this session; pb1361 (directive after comment lines, not on line 1) matches its .out at 2002.
